questions.question: Why are the intermediate goods NOT included in the National Income?

options.text: For the prevention of double accounting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For the prevention of double accounting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intermediate goods** are not included in the National Income to prevent double accounting.
 
• Including intermediate goods would lead to **double counting** because their value is already embedded in the final goods and services.
 
• National Income is a measure of the total value of **final goods and services** produced in an economy over a specific period.
 
• Counting intermediate goods separately would **inflate the National Income** figures inaccurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Intermediate goods are those goods that are used as inputs to produce other goods and services.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods include raw materials, components, and parts used in manufacturing.
 
• Final goods are those that are ready for consumption or investment and are included in the calculation of National Income.
 
• To accurately measure the economic activity and avoid overestimation, only the value of final goods and services is counted.

questions.question: Which amongst the following statements about the Indian social reformers of the 19th century is INCORRECT?

options.text: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
The Aligarh Movement was started by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in 1875.
Mahadev Govind Ranade is associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha

questions.solution:

__

• The **Aligarh Movement** was indeed started by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** in 1875 to promote modern education among Muslims.
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** is correctly associated with the **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha**, an organization aimed at promoting social and political reforms.
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati** founded the **Arya Samaj** in 1875, advocating for a return to the teachings of the Vedas and promoting social reform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Aligarh Movement** led to the establishment of the **Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College**, which later became the **Aligarh Muslim University**.
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** was also a judge and one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The **Arya Samaj** had a significant influence on Indian society, promoting values such as equality, social justice, and the importance of education.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECTLY stated social impact of the Green Revolution?

options.text: Primarily, the medium and large farmers were benefited
Worsened the condition of landless and marginal farmers
Only farmers involved in subsistence agriculture were benefitted
There was displacement of service caste group

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only farmers involved in subsistence agriculture were benefitted**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Only farmers involved in subsistence agriculture were benefitted** is an incorrect statement regarding the social impact of the Green Revolution.
 
• The Green Revolution primarily benefited medium and large-scale farmers who had the resources to invest in new technologies.
 
• It worsened the condition of landless and marginal farmers who could not compete with the increased productivity of larger farms.
 
• Service caste groups were displaced as traditional agricultural practices and labor requirements changed.
 
• The Green Revolution led to increased disparities in income and land ownership, favoring those who were already better off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• Key elements included the development of high-yielding varieties of cereal grains, expansion of irrigation infrastructure, modernization of management techniques, distribution of hybridized seeds, synthetic fertilizers, and pesticides to farmers.
 
• While it significantly increased food production and reduced hunger, it also led to social and economic inequalities and environmental issues such as soil degradation and pesticide contamination.
 
• The Green Revolution is often credited with helping to avoid widespread famine and feeding millions of people, but its benefits were not uniformly distributed across all segments of the population.

questions.question: The 42ⁿd Amendment of the Indian Constitution (1976) states that India is a/an ____________ nation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**secular**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 42nd Amendment of the Indian Constitution, enacted in 1976, added the term **secular** to the Preamble, declaring India as a secular nation.
 
• A secular state is one that does not uphold any religion as the state religion and treats all religions equally.
 
• This amendment aimed to emphasize the commitment of the Indian state to maintain neutrality in religious matters and ensure that all citizens are treated equally, irrespective of their religion.
 
• The amendment also added the terms "socialist" and "integrity" to the Preamble, among other significant changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 42nd Amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its comprehensive nature and the wide-ranging changes it introduced.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• Besides the Preamble, the amendment also made significant changes to the Constitution in areas such as the judiciary, the executive, and the federal structure.
 
• The amendment has been subject to criticism and subsequent modifications, particularly through the 44th Amendment, which aimed to restore some of the checks and balances that were altered by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.question:
Choose the correct statement about the peninsular rivers.

a. The Narmada rises in the Malwa plateau.

b. The Godavari rises from the slopes of the Western Ghats near Nashik.

c. The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh.

d. The Krishna rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only b, c and d**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Only b, c, and d** are correct statements about the peninsular rivers of India.
 
• The Godavari rises from the slopes of the Western Ghats near Nashik.
 
• The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh.
 
• The Krishna rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar.
 
• The Narmada, however, does not rise in the Malwa plateau; it rises in the Amarkantak plateau.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The peninsular rivers of India are primarily rain-fed and have a seasonal flow pattern.
 
• These rivers flow through the Deccan Plateau and are characterized by their mature stage, having wider valleys and lower gradients.
 
• Major peninsular rivers include the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, and Mahanadi, which flow eastwards into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Narmada and Tapti are notable exceptions as they flow westwards into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question:
Who among the following are eligible for free legal aid under the National Legal Services Authority?

A. A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.

B. A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution

C. An industrial workman

D. A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disasters

E. To file any case in Supreme Court, if any person need free legal aid, the person’s annual income must be below 10 lakhs.

options.text: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, C and D only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A, B, C and D only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe** is eligible for free legal aid under the National Legal Services Authority.
 
• **A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution** is also eligible for free legal aid.
 
• **An industrial workman** qualifies for free legal aid as per the National Legal Services Authority.
 
• **A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of mass disasters** is eligible for free legal aid.
 
• To file any case in the Supreme Court, if any person needs free legal aid, the person's annual income must be below a certain threshold, but **the specific limit of 10 lakhs is not mentioned under the eligibility criteria of the National Legal Services Authority.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, to provide free legal services to the weaker sections of the society and to organize Lok Adalats for amicable settlement of disputes.
 
• The **objective of NALSA** is to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
 
• The criteria for providing free legal aid include several categories of persons such as women and children, disabled persons, victims of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster, and persons in custody, among others.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT an advantage of privatisation?

options.text: Additional source of revenue for the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduced competition**__

__
 
• **Reduced competition** is not considered an advantage of privatisation.
 
• Privatisation typically aims to increase competition by introducing private players into sectors previously dominated by state-run enterprises.
 
• Increased competition can lead to better services, more innovation, and greater efficiency in the market.
 
• Other advantages of privatisation include generating additional revenue for the government, reducing political interference, and improving overall performance of the enterprises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership, property or business from the government to the private sector.
 
• It is often part of broader economic reforms aimed at improving efficiency and productivity.
 
• Privatisation can also help in reducing the fiscal burden on the government and in fostering a more competitive economic environment.
 
• However, it is important to carefully regulate privatised sectors to ensure fair competition and prevent monopolistic practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Aluminium Sulphate is commonly used in water purification, paper manufacturing, and as a mordant in dyeing and printing textiles.
 
• It is also used in the food industry as a firming agent.
 
• The molecular weight of Aluminium Sulphate Al₂(SO₄)₃ is approximately 342.15 g/mol.
 
• When dissolved in water, it dissociates into aluminium ions (Al³⁺) and sulphate ions (SO₄²⁻).

questions.question: Which bacteria have a thick cell wall with several layers of peptidoglycan and teichoic acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Staphylococcus aureus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Staphylococcus aureus** has a thick cell wall composed of several layers of peptidoglycan and teichoic acid.
 
• The thick peptidoglycan layer provides structural strength and rigidity to the bacterial cell wall.
 
• Teichoic acid, which is embedded in the cell wall, plays a role in cell wall maintenance and ion regulation.
 
• These features are characteristic of **Gram-positive bacteria**, to which Staphylococcus aureus belongs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salmonella enterica**, **Pseudomonas aeruginosa**, and **Escherichia coli** are examples of **Gram-negative bacteria**, which have a thinner peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane.
 
• Gram-positive bacteria, like Staphylococcus aureus, stain violet in the Gram staining procedure due to their thick peptidoglycan layer.
 
• The structure of the cell wall in Gram-positive bacteria makes them more susceptible to certain antibiotics, such as penicillin, which targets peptidoglycan synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following is the longest Highway Tunnel in India (as of 2022)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Tunnel**__

• The tunnel is situated in the state of **Himachal Pradesh** and connects **Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley**.
 
• It is named after the former Prime Minister of India, **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**.
 
• The tunnel is **9.02 km long** and is built under the **Rohtang Pass** in the eastern Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas.
 
• It was inaugurated on **3rd October 2020** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• The Atal Tunnel significantly reduces the travel time between Manali and Leh, providing all-weather connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Pir Panjal Tunnel**, also known as the **Banihal Railway Tunnel**, is the second-longest tunnel in India.
 
• The **Karbude Tunnel** is a railway tunnel located in Maharashtra on the Konkan Railway line.
 
• The **Jawahar Tunnel** is a road tunnel in Jammu and Kashmir, connecting Banihal with Qazigund.
 
• The construction of the Atal Tunnel was a significant engineering challenge due to the harsh weather conditions and difficult terrain.
 
• The tunnel is equipped with modern safety features such as CCTV cameras, fire hydrants, and emergency exits.

questions.question: The Battle of Kannauj was fought between Sher Shah Suri and the Mughals led by _______________.

• After losing to Sher Shah Suri, Humayun went into exile for about 15 years.
 
• He later regained the throne with the help of the Persian Empire in 1555, shortly before his death in 1556.
 
• Sher Shah Suri is known for his administrative reforms and the introduction of the currency system called "Rupiya."

questions.question: According to Dr. BR Ambedkar’s views, which of the following is the key feature of the Directive Principles of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Novel feature**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Dr. BR Ambedkar, the **Directive Principles** of the Constitution are considered a **novel feature**.
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Directive Principles are included in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• These principles reflect the ideals that the State should strive to achieve, such as securing a social order based on justice, minimizing inequalities, and ensuring the right to work, education, and public assistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and are inspired by the principles of social justice outlined in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• These principles aim to establish a welfare state in India and ensure that the government works towards the betterment of its citizens.
 
• Although not enforceable by law, Directive Principles are considered essential in the governance and policy-making process of the country.
 
• They serve as a yardstick for measuring the performance of the government and guide the legislative and executive actions at all levels of governance.
